description: Three quantizers sharing one set of note buttons, each with an attenuverter on its input, and a nudge and a transpose control over all three

params.text: Sets how much of the voltage at the jack beside it reaches the quantizer, from full inversion through nothing at the middle to full; at the middle the row holds one note
Adds a note to the scale, or takes it away; the twelve buttons are a single octave of a piano keyboard stood on end
Shifts every row up or down after quantizing, by up to twelve semitones either way
Shifts every row up or down before quantizing, by up to 2V either way

inputs.text: The voltage to quantize for this row; it is scaled by the attenuverter beside it and then held between -10V and 10V

outputs.text: The nearest note of the chosen scale to this row's input, 1V per octave

notes: the black screen on each row shows the note that row is putting out, and it does not take the transpose setting into account
with no note buttons on at all the outputs hold their last value, 0V on a new module; the manual says they round to the nearest C, which is no longer what the code does
a row with nothing patched to its input puts out 0V
